title: Multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial assessing the efficacy and safety of proton pump inhibitor lansoprazole in infants with symptoms of gastroesophageal reflux disease
authors: Orenstein SR, Hassall E, Furmaga-Jablonska W, Atkinson S, Raanan M
population: Infants aged 1 to 12 months with symptoms attributed to gastro-oesophageal reflux persisting after at least 1 week of non-drug management
funder: The article's funding statement was not read because the publisher page could not be accessed. Registry NCT00324974: lead sponsor Takeda (industry); responsible party Sr. VP Clinical Sciences, Takeda Global Research & Development Center; study director a Takeda medical director.
result: Responders (at least 50% reduction in feeding-related crying): 44 of 81 (54%) with lansoprazole and 44 of 81 (54%) with placebo; no difference in any secondary efficacy measure. Treatment-emergent adverse events 62% against 46% (P = .058). Serious adverse events, particularly lower respiratory tract infections, in 10 infants on lansoprazole against 2 on placebo (P = .032).
